THE NATIONAL INTEREST: While the World Wants Oil, Mexico Stays on the Sidelines
July 3, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The National Interest scolds Mexico for "staying on the sidelines" while other countries drill for export markets. 🇲🇽 Sheinbaum isn't chasing global barrels — she's stabilizing Pemex for domestic supply and building toward 70% clean power by 2030. Not maximizing oil exports during a climate crisis is a choice, not a failure.

The piece leads with Pemex's $2.6B Q1 loss but never mentions Mexico's renewable buildout or that oil-export maximalism is exactly what the planet can't afford.

• "decades of mismanagement of the oil sector"
• "content to let other countries go after global markets"

🇲🇽📈 <u>THE SUPERPESO CLIMBS AGAIN — ON AMERICA'S WEAKNESS</u>

The peso closed at 17.47 per dollar, strengthening again — this time because the US jobs report collapsed: just 57,000 new jobs in June, roughly half the forecast, with May revised down from 172,000 to 129,000. Bets on Fed rate cuts sank the dollar. Mexico's currency keeps gaining on Washington's cooling economy, not on any trouble of its own.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S OPPOSITION CAUGHT PUSHING AN AI DEEPFAKE TO SMEAR AMLO</u>

Mexico's opposition got caught circulating an AI-generated fake video to attack AMLO — so blatant that even figures in their own camp called for it to be taken down. The family targeted called the smear "indignant and shameful," demanded evidence or a public apology, and is weighing legal action. When you have no record to run on, you manufacture one.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SAME FUNDERS, SAME SCRIPT: THE SOFT COUP AGAINST SHEINBAUM</u>

Contralínea maps the destabilization network aimed at Sheinbaum: USAID and NED money, the Atlas Network, Vargas Llosa's foundation, CPAC, and the PAN old guard — Calderón, Fox, Cortés — running what the report calls "a new offensive phase of limited chaos," the same playbook deployed against Venezuela, Bolivia and Cuba. Same money, same NGOs, same script. Mexico has seen this movie.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>DEATH BY PAPERWORK: THE NETWORK CHOKING THE TREN MAYA</u>

A Contralínea investigation finds 70 environmental cases against the Tren Maya still open — 24 of them on the main line — kept alive for up to 5 years, with the agency pushing "millionaire fines" routed toward a private trust tied to Julia Carabias and José Sarukhán, both longtime opponents of the project. Officials insist the permits are "100% in place." The files just never close.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US SEIZES 138 GUNS BOUND FOR MEXICO — A DROP IN AN OCEAN IT CREATED</u>

US Ambassador Ronald Johnson announced Washington intercepted 138 firearms headed to Mexico from North Carolina, including two military-grade .50-caliber rifles: "every weapon seized is one less in the hands of criminals, making both our nations safer." True. Now account for the roughly 200,000 US guns that flood south every year — the ones Mexico has been suing American manufacturers over.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S BEST-EVER FIRST HALF FOR CAR SALES — AND CHINA IS DRIVING IT</u>

Mexicans bought 754,394 new vehicles in the first half of 2026 — up 5.31% and the highest first half since records began in 2005, topping the old 2017 peak. June alone hit 126,778 units, the best June in nearly a decade. The engine? Chinese brands: Geely sales jumped 250% year-on-year. The "threat" Washington keeps naming turns out to be Mexican families finally affording a car.

🇲🇽📊 <u>471 BILLION PESOS SO FOOD AND MEDICINE STAY UNTAXED</u>

Mexico will forgo 1.67 trillion pesos in tax revenue in 2026 — roughly 4.5% of GDP — and the single biggest piece, 471 billion pesos, is the 0% IVA that keeps food and medicine untaxed. That's not a loophole for the rich; it's a shield on every family's grocery basket and pharmacy shelf. When the state chooses not to tax tortillas and insulin, fiscal policy becomes social policy. (Data: SHCP, via El Financiero)

🇲🇽💜 <u>MEXICO CITY ENACTS A CARE SYSTEM LAW — FIRST OF ITS KIND</u>

Clara Brugada promulgated a Care System Law that treats childcare, eldercare and self-care as a collective responsibility — not the unpaid duty of women. It builds, in her words, "a welfare state with a feminist perspective," and for the first time puts a peso value on domestic labor in Mexico City, delivered on the ground through the Utopías and Casas de las Tres R. The care economy — the work that held everything up while going uncounted — finally gets counted.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>150 BILLION PESOS INTO THE GRID — PUBLIC POWER, PUBLIC WIRES</u>

Sheinbaum is putting 150 billion pesos into transmission and distribution, because "most interruptions come from overloaded lines," not a shortage of generation. After AMLO rebuilt public generating capacity through the CFE, the state is now modernizing the wires that carry that power to homes and businesses. Reliable electricity treated as a public good — financed and built by the state, not auctioned off.
